title: Pinto Beans
description: The quick little bean side: one can of whichever beans we have, garlic powder and a sprinkle of salt. Enough for the two of us at one dinner.
imageAlt: Reference photograph of cooked beans with herbs and a lime wedge in a pale stone bowl.
imageCaption: Reference photograph · beans with herbs and lime variation · serving inspiration
personalNote: They don’t have to be pinto beans. Use whichever can of beans we have or fancy.
advancePrep: Use ready-cooked canned beans. The heating time is a guide; follow the can and heat until steaming hot.

ingredients.name: Canned pinto beans or beans of choice
ingredients.note: Ready-cooked beans. Follow the can’s instructions about draining and heating.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.note: A small splash only if needed to keep the beans from catching.

steps.title: Get the beans bubbling
steps.description: Tip the canned beans into a small saucepan and heat on medium. Use their liquid, unless the can tells us to drain or rinse them; if needed, add a small splash of water so the beans can bubble without catching on the bottom.
ingredients: Canned pinto beans or beans of choice
steps.tip: These are already-cooked canned beans. Follow the heating instructions on the can.

steps.title: Add the garlic powder and salt
steps.description: Once they start bubbling, add the garlic powder and a sprinkle of salt. Stir it through and keep heating until the beans are steaming hot, following the can’s heating instructions.

steps.title: Serve alongside dinner
steps.description: Serve the beans alongside whichever version of the filling and other sides we’re having. One can is enough for the two of us at this dinner.

servingSuggestion: A side for 2 portions at one dinner, with tacos, fajitas, enchiladas or a Mexican bowl.
portionNote: The full batch is a side for 2 portions at one dinner. Make another can for the second night if we want beans again.
